text:
maya: heads-up — started seeing a weird latency bump on the speculative path when pairing Qwen drafts with Mixtral base today. baseline numbers were fine, but tail p99 inflated ~40ms on 2k seq workloads. anyone else?

sam: seen it in a couple traces, filing here rather than channel spam. suspect tokenizer alignment + kv cache misses?

jin: can you paste a trace? sequence lengths, model variants, and whether batching was enabled?

maya: quick paste: model routing = mixtral-8b-draft paired -> qwen-7b-compat fallback; batching disabled for these tests; tokenization diffs noticed: some long tokens split differently, causing soft-handshake to request a re-tokenize and drop kv acceptance.

alejandra: that re-tokenize path rings a bell — acceptance smoothing we added last month: if draft tokenizes differently we do a conservative rollback and re-run on the primary model. that avoids mismatch but adds latency.

sam: right — acceptance smoothing threshold currently is 0.85 (Jaccard-esque heuristic on token boundaries). if tokenizer mismatch drops below threshold we invalidate partial KV and fall back. that explains the spike.

perf-bot: perf profile attached: 
```
p99_latency_ms: 142.1 -> 182.4 (delta +28.5%)
cpu% spike on inference-worker: +15%
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.07 -> 0.31
speculative_accept_rate: 0.62 -> 0.44
```

maya: thanks. the kv_cache_miss_rate jump matches the re-tokenize invalidation hypothesis. curious why qwen <-> mixtral pair is particularly bad though. both are similar vocab sizes.

jin: two hypotheses: 1) RoPE scaling differences causing head alignment drift so cached keys mismatch, and 2) tokenization family mismatch — qwen uses byte-level behavior that splits mixtral tokens differently for long tails.

alejandra: also remember our kernel-selection bailout: when a model switches kernel family between draft and final (e.g., mixtral optimized kernels vs qwen ones) we currently flush certain fused-kernel states to avoid corruption. that adds a small constant overhead but should not trigger full kv invalidation. maybe the handshake logic is too conservative and conflates kernel-family changes with token mismatch.

sam: good point. i checked logs: kernel-family-change flag set true on those pairings, then we hit the path that invalidates the auxiliary KV shards. should we relax to per-head-dimension checks instead of blanket invalidate?

maya: proposal: add a "handshake smoothing" pass that estimates expected kv compatibility via a quick head-dim projection check. if projection similarity > 0.9 then allow optimistic reuse, else fall back. this would avoid the tokenization-only cases where kernel family differs but actual numeric layout is compatible.

ops-bot: note created: #INFR-8792 "handshake smoothing: projection pre-check for KV reuse" (assignee: jin)

jin: i like that. cheap check: sample first 64 tokens, run dot-product on cached K/V heads vs newly computed K/V in fp16 cheap-path and threshold. if below threshold, do conservative invalidate. otherwise allow speculative merge.

sam: question: how do we deal with tokenizer mismatch where token boundaries differ but semantic subwords align? we could do a token-boundary delta heuristic that weighs token overlap and head-projection similarity. both signals combined -> accept probability.

alejandra: yes — make it probabilistic acceptance. acceptance p = sigmoid(alpha * proj_sim + beta * token_overlap - gamma * kernel_change_flag). tune alpha/beta/gamma in experiments. defaults conservative but can be relaxed on low-latency SLAs.

maya: any concerns about correctness? we must never return corrupt sequences if we unsafely reuse KV. I want a safe fallback: if speculative accept later fails decoding verification (e.g., mismatched logits distribution), we immediately invalidate and re-run the suffix on the final model, but record the extra latency and count it as a regression in the rollout.

jin: agree — implement a cheap verification: after speculative merge, check top-k logits agreement for next token (k=4) with a small KL threshold; if KL > 0.5 then rollback. cheap because it's one-step compare.

sam: note: this interacts badly with batching heuristics. if we do per-request projection checks that are expensive, they can serialize batching. we should design this check to be vectorizable across batch and add it into the kernel selection path so it runs fused with key computation.

perf-bot: micro-benchmarks idea: run a synthetic workload with mixtral->qwen pair, vary token_overlap and proj_sim, measure p99 and speculative_accept_rate. quick numbers expected: relaxing gamma by 0.2 -> +8% accept rate and -20ms p99, failure rollback rate ~0.6%.

alejandra: timeline: i can prototype the projection-check shim and the KL verification in a branch. jin can add tuning harness for alpha/beta/gamma and perf-bot can run sweeps. aiming for canary in staging next week.

maya: perfect. last ask — log a new metric: handshake_decision_score and decision_reason so ops can slice by kernel-change/tokenizer-mismatch/proj_sim. helps with rollout observability.

ops-bot: metric requested: handshake_decision_score (float), handshake_decision_reason (enum: token_mismatch/kernel_change/proj_sim) — ticket added to metrics backlog.

sam: one more: RoPE drift note — also add a flag to treat RoPE scaling mismatches specially: if models have different rope base, downweight proj_sim since keys can be misaligned by rotation.

maya: noted. thanks team — I'll sync with jin + alejandra tomorrow and post a short experiment plan. :thumbsup:
